title: Close the gap to your partner
brief: Their #8 has the ball in midfield and is looking to play it out wide, away from you.
briefKid: Their midfielder is about to pass out wide, far from you.
question: The ball is out on the far wing: your full-back engages and your partner covers. Where do you go?
questionKid: Your partner went across to help. Where do you go?

takeaway.standard: With the ball wide, the back four slides across as one: the full-back engages, the near centre-back covers, and you, the far centre-back, slide across to about 10 m from your partner, goal-side of their #9.
takeaway.kid: Ball far away? Slide across near your partner, between their striker and our goal.

misconceptions.text: You held your spot while your partner went across to cover, so there is a big gap between you for their #9 to run into.
misconceptions.textKid: Your partner moved across. Slide over too, so there is no big gap.

misconceptions.text: You slid all the way across to your partner, so their #9 is free on your inside and one pass beats you both.
misconceptions.textKid: Too close to your partner! Stay between their striker and our goal.

misconceptions.text: You stepped out of the line toward the ball; your full-back and partner already have it covered, and their #9 can now run in behind you.
misconceptions.textKid: Don't chase the ball. Stay in line, between their striker and our goal.

notes: Re-authored for the far centre-back (U5). It used to be the far full-back tucking in with the ball on the far wing, a duplicate of m1-03 (same role, situation and answer). Now the full-back engages (keyed 3 m off the carrier; the automatic press arrived too late), the near centre-back covers behind it, the far full-back tucks in, and their #9 sits between our centre-backs, so the learner slides across to about 10 m from their partner, goal-side of the #9. Their #8 is keyed as a late runner (left automatic, it sprinted at up to 16 m/s into our back line).
